Cultural assumptions shift quickly. Words mean different things than they did a decade ago. Questions surface that once seemed settled. If I am not careful, I can either cling to old answers or drift without anchor.

‍

", "post-content-members-only": "

A Learning and Growth Orientation requires both humility and rootedness. It would be wrong to assume that experience guarantees wisdom, yet equally wrong to chase relevance without theological depth. Scripture does not change, but our understanding must deepen as context shifts.

So we study culture with open eyes while remaining grounded in Christ. We listen carefully to the stories people carry. We ask what questions they are actually asking. And we allow the Spirit to renew our minds. Remaining in Christ does not make us rigid. It makes us rooted enough to grow. In that growth, we discover fresh ways to love people without abandoning truth.
